---

I changed the default page size for `GET /parcels` from 50 to 100.

**What changed:**
- `api/pagination.py:8`: `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 100`
- `tests/test_pagination.py`: `test_default_page_size` now expects 100

**What I checked first:**
- Nothing else in the project reads `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`, so nothing else in this code changes.
- 100 is still well below `MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 500`. No limit conflicts.
- I ran the pagination test and the full test suite after the edit. I'll paste the results right below. If anything fails, I'll show you the output and won't call this done.

**What this means outside the code, for you and your manager:**
- Any client that calls `/parcels` without setting a page size will now get up to twice as many rows per response. That means larger payloads and a bit more database work for each call.
- Some clients may expect 50 items per page. For example, a client might count pages or check whether a page is full to decide whether to fetch the next one. Clients that read the pagination links or cursor won't be affected. Clients that hard-code 50 could skip or duplicate items. I can only see this repo, so I can't check those clients.
- The fix is fast if something goes wrong: change one constant back and redeploy. If you want extra safety, ship it on its own, not bundled with other changes, so rolling it back can't pull anything else back with it.
